subject: Request: additional promo credits after trial disruptions
messages:
From: Tom Sanders <tom@shadowtech.io>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: additional promo credits after trial disruptions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking a look. We signed up two weeks ago to evaluate Redwood for a customer-facing feature. During our trial window we had two unexpected incidents on our side (internal infra outage + CI pipeline misconfiguration) that consumed a bunch of tokens while the team was troubleshooting. That left us short of meaningful eval time.

Is there any chance you can top up our trial credits or extend the trial window so we can finish the evaluation? Our team is small — this pilot matters for our Q4 roadmap.

Attaching prod logs that show the outage windows. Happy to provide billing/usage details.

Thanks,
Tom Sanders
Head of ML Platform
ShadowTech
Attachments: prod_logs.zip (archive)
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Sanders <tom@shadowtech.io>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: additional promo credits after trial disruptions

Hi Tom —

Sorry to hear about the outages — appreciate the logs. Before I can approve an extension or top-up I need a couple of quick clarifications:

- Can you confirm the organization domain(s) used for the trial (any secondary accounts)?
- Roughly how many distinct users/engineers hit the API during the trial window?
- Do you have a HubSpot or PO/Deal id we can tie this to?

We do have protections in the trial credit flow to prevent repeated stacking and to detect multi-account patterns; if you used multiple sign-ups we may need a short review. If everything looks clean I'm able to offer a one-time courtesy extension for evaluation.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Manager, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Evelyn —

Thanks, quick answers below:
- Primary domain: shadowtech.io. We also used shadow-team1@shadowtech.io for a couple of experiments.
- Users: 4 engineers (two were running large eval batches during the outage).
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/8772 (same link you probably have).

If you need any more logs or a short call, let me know. We can consolidate access if that helps.

—Tom
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: additional promo credits after trial disruptions

Folks — forwarding a customer appeal from ShadowTech. They claim legitimate outage usage but they also mention multiple secondary accounts. Can someone pull a quick abuse check and billing export? Key asks:

- Verify number of distinct accounts tied to shadowtech.io and any related emails (shadow-team1@...).
- Check IP overlap and payment method fingerprints.
- Confirm whether promo code PROMO-TRIAL-50 was applied multiple times across accounts.

I can escalate an exception if the signals look clean. If there's reuse/automation we should deny and provide the standard policy response. Marcus — can you own the analysis? Priyom / Rachel please add any telemetry (rate-limit hits, suspicious agent patterns).

Thanks,
Evelyn
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: additional promo credits after trial disruptions

Quick summary from the abuse/billing check (attached export: billing_export_2027-08-28.csv):

- Accounts: we see three accounts tied to shadowtech.io and two service addresses (shadow-team1@shadowtech.io, shadow-ci@shadowtech.io).
- IP overlap: three distinct accounts share an originating IP (52.11.33.7) during the trial period — consistent with same site/office.
- Promo usage: the promotional trial code PROMO-TRIAL-50 was applied to two different account IDs. Our promo rules allow one use per legal entity; multiple uses trigger the reuse detection.
- Behavioral signals: one of the accounts executed a very large, automated eval batch with repeated short sessions that look like scripted retries (high-frequency start/stop).

Recommendation: deny broad extension and surface standardized policy wording. Offer a limited, one-time courtesy — e.g., 250 free credits and a week-long evaluation window — contingent on consolidation of accounts under a single org and an attestation that no additional new accounts will be created to bypass policy. That keeps us consistent with precedent while giving them an opportunity to finish evaluation.

Attached: billing_export_2027-08-28.csv (CSV export), notes: SUP-4927.

—Marcus
Senior Manager, Risk & Revenue Operations
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Sanders <tom@shadowtech.io>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: additional promo credits after trial disruptions

Tom —

Thanks for the prompt details and the logs. We completed our review with RevOps. Short version: we detected multiple accounts tied to shadowtech.io and two uses of the trial promo code, which triggers our reuse protections.

That said, we want to help you complete the evaluation. As a one-time courtesy we can:

- Add 250 free credits to a single consolidated account (we'll coordinate a single admin email).
- Extend the evaluation window by 7 days.

Conditions: you must consolidate the secondary accounts (shadow-team1@shadowtech.io, shadow-ci@shadowtech.io) under one org user and confirm consolidation in writing. If we detect attempts to create additional trial accounts, we will rescind the courtesy.

If that works, reply with the admin email you want us to use and I'll open the HubSpot deal and ticket (SUP-4927) for the credit top-up.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Manager, Strategic Sales
